B.2 Shallow recurrent neural network (RNN) representation

The conditional independence property in the state |ψ⟩\left|\psi\right\rangle also yields a recurrent neural network representations of |ψ⁡(x)||\psi(x)| with 𝒪⁡(logDΛ⁡(n))\mathcal{O}(\log^{D_{\Lambda}}(n)) memory in a DD-dimensional lattice. As we discuss, the RNN architecture also incorporates a DΛD_{\Lambda}-dimensional design [34]. To show this, analogous to the proof of Theorem B.3, we start with a one-dimensional chain.

One-dimensional chain:

As before, we divide the chain into contiguous sets 𝖠1,𝖠2,…,𝖠M\mathsf{A}_{1},\mathsf{A}_{2},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{M} where each |𝖠j|=2​ℓ0⋅log⁡(n)|\mathsf{A}_{j}|=2\ell_{0}\cdot\log(n). We now show that one can factorize the overall probability p𝖠1,⋯,𝖠Mp_{\mathsf{A}_{1},\cdots,\mathsf{A}_{M}} into the product ∏j=1Mp𝖠j|𝖠j−1\prod_{j=1}^{M}p_{\mathsf{A}_{j}|\mathsf{A}_{j-1}} with 𝖠0=∅\mathsf{A}_{0}=\emptyset. This follows from

||∏j=1Mp𝖠j|𝖠<j−∏j=1Mp𝖠j|𝖠j−1||1\displaystyle{\left|\hskip-1.59016pt\left|\prod_{j=1}^{M}p_{\mathsf{A}_{j}|\mathsf{A}_{<j}}-\prod_{j=1}^{M}p_{\mathsf{A}_{j}|\mathsf{A}_{j-1}}\right|\hskip-1.59016pt\right|}_{1}
≤∑k=1M−1||∏j=1kp𝖠j|𝖠<j⋅(p𝖠k+1|𝖠≤k−p𝖠k+1​𝖠k)⋅∏j=kM−2p𝖠j+2|𝖠j+1||1\displaystyle\leq\sum_{k=1}^{M-1}{\left|\hskip-1.59016pt\left|\prod_{j=1}^{k}p_{\mathsf{A}_{j}|\mathsf{A}_{<j}}\cdot(p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1}|\mathsf{A}_{\leq k}}-p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1}\mathsf{A}_{k}})\cdot\prod_{j=k}^{M-2}p_{\mathsf{A}_{j+2}|\mathsf{A}_{j+1}}\right|\hskip-1.59016pt\right|}_{1}
≤∑k=1M−1||∏j=1kp𝖠j|𝖠<j⋅(p𝖠k+1|𝖠≤k−p𝖠k+1|𝖠k)||1\displaystyle\leq\sum_{k=1}^{M-1}{\left|\hskip-1.59016pt\left|\prod_{j=1}^{k}p_{\mathsf{A}_{j}|\mathsf{A}_{<j}}\cdot(p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1}|\mathsf{A}_{\leq k}}-p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1}|\mathsf{A}_{k}})\right|\hskip-1.59016pt\right|}_{1}
=∑k=1M−1||p𝖠k⋅p𝖠k−1,⋯,𝖠1|𝖠k⋅(p𝖠k+1,𝖠k−1,…,𝖠1|𝖠kp𝖠k−1,⋯,𝖠1|𝖠k−p𝖠k+1|𝖠k)||1\displaystyle=\sum_{k=1}^{M-1}{\left|\hskip-1.59016pt\left|p_{\mathsf{A}_{k}}\cdot p_{\mathsf{A}_{k-1},\cdots,\mathsf{A}_{1}|\mathsf{A}_{k}}\cdot\left(\frac{p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1},\mathsf{A}_{k-1},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{1}|\mathsf{A}_{k}}}{p_{\mathsf{A}_{k-1},\cdots,\mathsf{A}_{1}|\mathsf{A}_{k}}}-p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1}|\mathsf{A}_{k}}\right)\right|\hskip-1.59016pt\right|}_{1}
=∑k=1M−1𝔼𝗔𝒌​‖p𝖠k+1,𝖠k−1,…,𝖠1|𝗔𝒌−p𝖠k+1|𝗔𝒌⋅p𝖠k−1,⋯,𝖠1|𝗔𝒌‖1⏟≤n−(ℓ0/ξ−c0)≤n−(ℓ0/ξ−c0−1).\displaystyle=\sum_{k=1}^{M-1}\underbrace{\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{\mathsf{A}_{k}}}{|\hskip-1.59016pt|p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1},\mathsf{A}_{k-1},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{1}|\bm{\mathsf{A}_{k}}}-p_{\mathsf{A}_{k+1}|\bm{\mathsf{A}_{k}}}\cdot p_{\mathsf{A}_{k-1},\cdots,\mathsf{A}_{1}|\bm{\mathsf{A}_{k}}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{1}}_{\leq n^{-(\ell_{0}/\xi-c_{0})}}\leq n^{-(\ell_{0}/\xi-c_{0}-1)}. (25)

The last line is a consequence of the approximate conditional independence in Definition II.1 after recognizing 𝖠=∪j=1k−1𝖠j\mathsf{A}=\cup_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathsf{A}_{j}, 𝖡=𝖠k\mathsf{B}=\mathsf{A}_{k}, and 𝖢=∪j=k+1n𝖠j\mathsf{C}=\cup_{j=k+1}^{n}\mathsf{A}_{j} and choosing a suitable constant c0c_{0} such that poly⁡(𝖠,𝖢)≤nc0\operatorname{poly}(\mathsf{A},\mathsf{C})\leq n^{c_{0}}.

As shown in Figure 1, the recurrent neural network consists of a cascade of cells each computing the probability of a variable conditioned on the value of the variables in the previous cells. Define x1(k),⋯,xM′(k)x^{(k)}_{1},\cdots,x^{(k)}_{M^{\prime}} to be the set of variables in each subset 𝖠k\mathsf{A}_{k}, where M′:=2​ℓ0​log⁡(n)M^{\prime}:=2\ell_{0}\log(n). We now focus on a subset of cells that computes the conditional probabilities

p(x1(k),⋯,xM′(k)|x1(k−1),⋯,xM′(k−1))=∏i=1M′p(xi(k)|x<i(k),x≤M′(k−1))p(x^{(k)}_{1},\cdots,x^{(k)}_{M^{\prime}}|x^{(k-1)}_{1},\cdots,x^{(k-1)}_{M^{\prime}})=\prod_{i=1}^{M^{\prime}}p(x^{(k)}_{i}|x^{(k)}_{<i},x^{(k-1)}_{\leq M^{\prime}})

for some k∈[M]k\in[M]. The cell that computes p⁡(xi(k)|x<i(k−1),x≤M′(k−1))p(x^{(k)}_{i}|x^{(k-1)}_{<i},x^{(k-1)}_{\leq M^{\prime}}) takes as input xi−1(k)x^{(k)}_{i-1} and a hidden memory state hi−1(k)h^{(k)}_{i-1}. It then outputs an updated memory

hi(k)=fh​(xi−1(k),hi−1(k))\displaystyle h^{(k)}_{i}=f_{h}(x^{(k)}_{i-1},h^{(k)}_{i-1}) (26)

and the conditional probability

p⁡(xi(k)|x<i(k),x≤M′(k−1))=fp​(hi(k)).p(x^{(k)}_{i}|x^{(k)}_{<i},x^{(k-1)}_{\leq M^{\prime}})=f_{p}(h^{(k)}_{i}).

The updated memory can be simply set hi(k)=(x<i(k),x≤M′(k−1))h^{(k)}_{i}=(x^{(k)}_{<i},x^{(k-1)}_{\leq M^{\prime}}) which involves 𝒪⁡(log⁡(n))\mathcal{O}(\log(n)) many variables compared to Ω⁡(n)\Omega(n) variables needed for general nn-variable distributions.

The function fp​(hi(k))f_{p}(h^{(k)}_{i}) is constructed similar to the proof of Theorem B.3 which yields a shallow feedforward neural network of depth 𝒪⁡(log⁡log⁡(n))\mathcal{O}(\log\log(n)) and width poly⁡(n)\operatorname{poly}(n) that computes p⁡(xi(k)|x<i(k),x≤M′(k−1))p(x^{(k)}_{i}|x^{(k)}_{<i},x^{(k-1)}_{\leq M^{\prime}}) up to 1poly⁡(n)\frac{1}{\operatorname{poly}(n)} multiplicative error. An argument similar to the one leading to (25) shows the overall factorized distribution ∏k=1M∏i=1M′p⁡(xi(k)|x<i(k),x≤M′(k−1))\prod_{k=1}^{M}\prod_{i=1}^{M^{\prime}}p(x^{(k)}_{i}|x^{(k)}_{<i},x^{(k-1)}_{\leq M^{\prime}}) can be computed with this recurrent architecture within 1poly⁡(n)\frac{1}{\operatorname{poly}(n)} error in ℓ1\ell_{1} distance. Combined with the error bound in (25), this yields a shallow recurrent neural network that computes and samples from p⁡(x1,…,xn)p(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) up to 1poly⁡(n)\frac{1}{\operatorname{poly}(n)} error in ℓ1\ell_{1} distance.

𝑫𝚲\bm{D_{\Lambda}}-dimensional lattice:

The one-dimensional construction above can be generalized to the DΛD_{\Lambda}-dimensional lattice Λ=ℤDΛ\Lambda=\mathbb{Z}^{D_{\Lambda}} by a proper choice of regions 𝖠k\mathsf{A}_{k} to condition on in each RNN cell. We first consider the DΛ=2D_{\Lambda}=2 lattice and partition it into regions ∪k=1M𝖠k\cup_{k=1}^{M}\mathsf{A}_{k} with a ‘snake’ ordering shown in Figure 7 and a 2D RNN architecture such as the one considered in [34]. The DΛ>2D_{\Lambda}>2 case follows from a similar argument. Analogous to the proof of Theorem B.1, we consider the neighborhood ∂𝖠k\partial\mathsf{A}_{k} of each subset 𝖠k\mathsf{A}_{k}. In the proof of (25) for the one-dimensional case, it suffices to factorize the distribution into a product of conditional distributions p⁡(𝖠k|𝖠k−1)p(\mathsf{A}_{k}|\mathsf{A}_{k-1}) since 𝖠k−1\mathsf{A}_{k-1} shields 𝖠k\mathsf{A}_{k} from variables in 𝖠≤k−2\mathsf{A}_{\leq k-2}. In the two-dimensional lattice, the factorization is in terms of distributions p⁡(𝖠k|∂𝖠k∩𝖠<k)p(\mathsf{A}_{k}|\partial\mathsf{A}_{k}\cap\mathsf{A}_{<k}) since we now need ∂𝖠k∩𝖠<k\partial\mathsf{A}_{k}\cap\mathsf{A}_{<k} to shield 𝖠k\mathsf{A}_{k} from the previous subsets and be able to to apply the conditional independence property in Definition II.1. Since the number of regions in ∂𝖠k∩𝖠<k\partial\mathsf{A}_{k}\cap\mathsf{A}_{<k} is a constant, the remainder of the proof is analogous to the one-dimensional case. We note that the ordering in which the distribution p⁡(x1,…,xn)p(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) is factorized is the ‘reverse’ of the construction in Theorem B.1. The regions ∂𝖠k∩𝖠<k\partial\mathsf{A}_{k}\cap\mathsf{A}_{<k} have a two-dimensional geometry. However, conventional 1D RNNs, as shown in Figure 1(b), map 2D regions to 1D configurations, often disrupting spatial locality and requiring poly⁡(n)\operatorname{poly}(n)-sized hidden memory states to capture the resulting non-local information. To better align the RNN architecture with 2D geometry, the authors in [34] proposes a design where hidden memory states propagate vertically as well as horizontally (see their Fig. 5(b)). In other words, instead of following (26), the updated memory state hi​j(k)h^{(k)}_{ij} in the RNN cell at row ii and column jj within the kk’th region 𝖠k\mathsf{A}_{k} now satisfies

hi​j(k)=fh​(xi−1,j(k),hi−1,j(k),xi,j−1(k),hi,j−1(k)).\displaystyle h_{ij}^{(k)}=f_{h}(x_{i-1,j}^{(k)},h_{i-1,j}^{(k)},x_{i,j-1}^{(k)},h_{i,j-1}^{(k)}).

Extensions of this architecture to higher dimensions follow naturally. These generalized RNN wavefunctions allow the computation of conditional probabilities p⁡(𝖠k|∂𝖠k∩𝖠<k)p(\mathsf{A}_{k}|\partial\mathsf{A}_{k}\cap\mathsf{A}_{<k}) using 𝒪⁡(logDΛ⁡(n))\mathcal{O}(\log^{D_{\Lambda}}(n)) dimensional hidden memory.

Appendix C From conditional independence to area law

Here, we establish Theorem II.4, which shows that approximate conditional independence in non-negative quantum states leads to an entanglement area law for such states.

Theorem C.1 (Approximate conditional independence implies area law).

Consider an nn-qudit sign-free state |ψ⟩∈ℂd⊗⋯⊗ℂd\left|\psi\right\rangle\in\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb{C}^{d} on a lattice. Suppose the measurement distribution of this state satisfies the approximate conditional independence property (4) for a given tripartition 𝖠∪𝖡∪𝖢=[n]\mathsf{A}\cup\mathsf{B}\cup\mathsf{C}=[n] of the lattice such that 𝖠∩𝖢=∅\mathsf{A}\cap\mathsf{C}=\emptyset. The von Neumann entropy of the reduced state ρ𝖠\rho_{\mathsf{A}} in region 𝖠\mathsf{A} is upper bounded by

S⁡(ρ𝖠)≤𝒪⁡(|𝖡|),S(\rho_{\mathsf{A}})\leq\mathcal{O}(|\mathsf{B}|),

which up to log⁡(|𝖠|)\log(|\mathsf{A}|) factors implies an area law S⁡(ρ𝖠)≤𝒪⁡(|∂𝖠|⋅log⁡(|∂𝖠|)𝐶𝐿𝑂𝑆𝐸S(\rho_{\mathsf{A}})\leq\mathcal{O}(|\partial\mathsf{A}|\cdot\log(|\partial\mathsf{A}|).

Proof.

Consider the following state |ϕ⟩\left|\phi\right\rangle defined by

|ϕ⟩:=∑x𝖠,x𝖡,x𝖢p⁡(x𝖡)⋅p⁡(x𝖠|x𝖡)⋅p⁡(x𝖢|x𝖡)⋅|x𝖠,x𝖡,x𝖢⟩,\displaystyle\left|\phi\right\rangle:=\sum_{x_{\mathsf{A}},x_{\mathsf{B}},x_{\mathsf{C}}}\sqrt{p(x_{\mathsf{B}})\cdot p(x_{\mathsf{A}}|x_{\mathsf{B}})\cdot p(x_{\mathsf{C}}|x_{\mathsf{B}})}\cdot\left|x_{\mathsf{A}},x_{\mathsf{B}},x_{\mathsf{C}}\right\rangle, (27)

where the sum is over x𝖠∈[d]|𝖠|x_{\mathsf{A}}\in[d]^{|\mathsf{A}|}, x𝖡∈[d]|𝖡|x_{\mathsf{B}}\in[d]^{|\mathsf{B}|}, and x𝖢∈[d]|𝖢|x_{\mathsf{C}}\in[d]^{|\mathsf{C}|}. If the ground state |ψ⟩\left|\psi\right\rangle satisfies the conditional independence exactly, then it would be equal to the state |ϕ⟩\left|\phi\right\rangle. The proof of area law includes two steps:

  1. 1.

    First, we show that the entropies of the reduced states

    ρ𝖠=tr𝖡𝖢⁡(|ψ⟩​⟨ψ|)andσ𝖠=tr𝖡𝖢⁡(|ϕ⟩​⟨ϕ|)\rho_{\mathsf{A}}=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathsf{BC}}(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)\quad\text{and}\quad\sigma_{\mathsf{A}}=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathsf{BC}}(|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|)

By combining these two steps, we arrive at the area law for the entanglement entropy S⁡(ρ𝖠)S(\rho_{\mathsf{A}}).

Step 1:

We begin by bounding the overlap ⟨ϕ|ψ⟩\left\langle\phi\middle|\psi\right\rangle

⟨ϕ|ψ⟩\displaystyle\left\langle\phi\middle|\psi\right\rangle =𝔼𝒙𝖡​[∑x𝖠,x𝖢p⁡(x𝖠,x𝖢|𝒙𝖡)⋅p⁡(xA|𝒙B)⋅p⁡(xC|𝒙B)]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}\left[\sum_{x_{\mathsf{A}},x_{\mathsf{C}}}\sqrt{p(x_{\mathsf{A}},x_{\mathsf{C}}|\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}})}\cdot\sqrt{p(x_{A}|\bm{x}_{B})\cdot p(x_{C}|\bm{x}_{B})}\right]
=𝔼𝒙𝖡​F1/2​(p𝖠,𝖢|𝒙𝖡,p𝖠|𝒙𝖡⊗p𝖢|𝒙𝖡)\displaystyle=\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}F^{1/2}\left(p_{{\mathsf{A}},{\mathsf{C}}|\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}},p_{{\mathsf{A}}|\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}\otimes p_{\mathsf{C}|\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}\right) (by definition of fidelity between distributions)

|S⁡(ρ𝖠)−S⁡(σ𝖠)|≤1poly⁡(|𝖠|).|S(\rho_{\mathsf{A}})-S(\sigma_{\mathsf{A}})|\leq\frac{1}{\operatorname{poly}(|{\mathsf{A}}|)}. (31)

in terms of the pure states

Appendix D Conditional independence in one-dimensional systems

Here, we establish several results concerning the decay of conditional mutual information for one-dimensional gapped Hamiltonians. We begin by formally defining entanglement swapping in Section D.2. Next, we prove the optimality of the Bell basis for entanglement swapping with qubits, as presented in Section D.4, and extend this result to the rotated cluster state in Section D.5. Finally, we analyze shallow random quantum circuits in 1D, demonstrating that they exhibit short-range conditional correlations in Section D.6.

D.1 Preliminaries on measures of entanglement

Definition D.1 (Concurrence of two-qubit states).

Given a pure two-qubit state |ϕ⟩𝖠𝖡=a|00⟩+b|01⟩+c|10⟩+d|11⟩\left|\phi\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}=a\left|00\right\rangle+b\left|01\right\rangle+c\left|10\right\rangle+d\left|11\right\rangle, we define its concurrence C⁡(ϕ𝖠𝖡)C(\phi_{\mathsf{AB}}) by

C⁡(ϕ𝖠𝖡)=2⋅|a​d−b​c|.\displaystyle C(\phi_{\mathsf{AB}})=2\cdot|ad-bc|. (37)

We can equivalently express the concurrence in terms of the reduced state ρ𝖠\rho_{\mathsf{A}} on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} as

C⁡(ϕ𝖠𝖡)=2⋅(tr⁡(ρ𝖠)2−tr⁡(ρ𝖠2)).\displaystyle C(\phi_{\mathsf{AB}})=\sqrt{2\cdot\left(\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\mathsf{A}})^{2}-\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\mathsf{A}}^{2})\right)}. (38)

More generally, the concurrence of a two-qubit mixed state ρ\rho is defined by

C⁡(ρ𝖠𝖡)=inf∑ipi⋅C⁡((ϕi)𝖠𝖡)\displaystyle C(\rho_{\mathsf{AB}})=\inf\sum_{i}p_{i}\cdot C\left((\phi_{i})_{\mathsf{AB}}\right) (39)

where the infimum is over all mixtures of pures states {pi,(ϕi)𝖠𝖡}\{p_{i},(\phi_{i})_{\mathsf{AB}}\} such that ρ𝖠𝖡=∑ipi⋅(ϕi)𝖠𝖡\rho_{\mathsf{AB}}=\sum_{i}p_{i}\cdot(\phi_{i})_{\mathsf{AB}}.

Fact D.1 (Closed form formula for concurrence, cf. [72]).

Given a two-qubit state ρ\rho, define

ρ~=(Y⊗Y)⋅ρ∗⋅(Y⊗Y)\displaystyle\widetilde{\rho}=(Y\otimes Y)\cdot\rho^{*}\cdot(Y\otimes Y) (40)

where ρ∗\rho^{*} is the complex conjugate of ρ\rho in the computational basis. Let α1≥α2≥α3≥α4\alpha_{1}\geq\alpha_{2}\geq\alpha_{3}\geq\alpha_{4} be the eigenvalues of the Hermitian operator ρ⋅ρ~⋅ρ\sqrt{\sqrt{\rho}\cdot\widetilde{\rho}\cdot\sqrt{\rho}}. The concurrence of ρ\rho satisfies

C⁡(ρ𝖠𝖡)=max⁡{0,α1−α2−α3−α4}.\displaystyle C(\rho_{\mathsf{AB}})=\max\{0,\alpha_{1}-\alpha_{2}-\alpha_{3}-\alpha_{4}\}. (41)
Fact D.2 (Entanglement entropy in terms of concurrence, cf. [36]).

Given a two-qubit state |ϕ⟩𝖠𝖡\left|\phi\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}, let ϕ𝖠\phi_{\mathsf{A}} be the reduced state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A}. The entanglement entropy S⁡(ϕ𝖠)S(\phi_{\mathsf{A}}) admits the following expression in terms of concurrence C⁡(ϕ𝖠𝖡)C(\phi_{\mathsf{AB}}):

S⁡(ϕ𝖠)=h⁡(1+1−C​(ϕ𝖠𝖡)22).\displaystyle S(\phi_{\mathsf{A}})=h\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{1-C(\phi_{\mathsf{AB}})^{2}}}{2}\right). (42)

Here h⁡(x)h(x) is the binary Shannon entropy defined by

h⁡(x)=−x​log⁡(x)−(1−x)​log⁡(1−x).\displaystyle h(x)=-x\log(x)-(1-x)\log(1-x). (43)
Definition D.2 (Entanglement of formation).

The Entanglement of formation for a state ρ𝖠𝖡\rho_{\mathsf{AB}} is defined by

EF​(ρ𝖠𝖡)=inf∑ipi⋅S⁡((ϕi)𝖠).\displaystyle E_{F}(\rho_{\mathsf{AB}})=\inf\sum_{i}p_{i}\cdot S\left((\phi_{i})_{\mathsf{A}}\right). (44)

The infimum in this expression is over all mixtures of pure states {pi,(ϕi)𝖠𝖡}\{p_{i},(\phi_{i})_{\mathsf{AB}}\} such that ρ𝖠𝖡=∑ipi⋅(ϕi)𝖠𝖡\rho_{\mathsf{AB}}=\sum_{i}p_{i}\cdot(\phi_{i})_{\mathsf{AB}}.

Fact D.3 (Entanglement of formation in terms of concurrence, cf. [72]).

The entanglement of formation of a two-qubit state ρ𝖠𝖡\rho_{\mathsf{AB}} satisfies

EF​(ρ𝖠𝖡)=h⁡(1+1−C​(ρ𝖠𝖡)22).\displaystyle E_{F}(\rho_{\mathsf{AB}})=h\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{1-C(\rho_{\mathsf{AB}})^{2}}}{2}\right). (45)

where h⁡(⋅)h(\cdot) is the binary Shannon entropy in (43) and the concurrence C⁡(ρ𝖠𝖡)C(\rho_{\mathsf{AB}}) is defined by the expression (39) in Definition D.1.

D.2 Entanglement swapping preliminaries

Definition D.3 (Bell basis).

Let d≥2d\geq 2 be an integer, and write ω=e2​π​i/d\omega=e^{2\pi i/d}. The generalized Bell basis is the set which contains a vector |𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅a,b⟩\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{a,b}\right\rangle in (ℂd)⊗2(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes 2} for each a,b∈{0,…,d−1}a,b\in\{0,\ldots,d-1\} defined as

|𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅a,b⟩=1d⋅∑x=0d−1ωa⋅x|x,x+b⟩,\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{a,b}\right\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\cdot\sum_{x=0}^{d-1}\omega^{a\cdot x}\left|x,x+b\right\rangle,

where addition is modulo dd.

By Definition D.3, the dd Schmidt coefficients of |𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅a,b⟩\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{a,b}\right\rangle are all 1/d1/\sqrt{d}. Hence, all of the Bell basis states are maximally entangled. A particular example of such states is the EPR state in ℂd\mathbb{C}^{d} given by

|𝖤𝖯𝖱d⟩:=|𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅0,0⟩=1d⋅∑x=0d−1|x,x⟩.\left|\mathsf{EPR}_{d}\right\rangle:=\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{0,0}\right\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\cdot\sum_{x=0}^{d-1}\left|x,x\right\rangle.

Before proceeding to introducing the entanglement swapping setup, we state and prove the following proposition which gives a decomposition of the four-party state |ψ⟩=|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣\left|\psi\right\rangle=\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}} in terms of the Bell basis.

Proposition D.4 (General state in Bell basis).

Consider the following two-qubit states |a⟩𝖠𝖡\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}} and |b⟩𝖢𝖣\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}:

|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣=(∑i=0d−1ai⋅|i,i⟩𝖠𝖡)⊗(∑j=0d−1bj⋅|j,j⟩𝖢𝖣).\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}=\Big(\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}a_{i}\cdot\left|i,i\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\Big)\otimes\Big(\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}b_{j}\cdot\left|j,j\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}\Big). (46)

Then, we have

|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣=1d⋅∑i,j=0d−1|𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅i,j⟩𝖡𝖢⊗(∑k=0d−1ω−i⋅k⋅ak⋅bk+j⋅|k,k+j⟩)𝖠𝖣.\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\cdot\sum_{i,j=0}^{d-1}\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{i,j}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes\Big(\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}\omega^{-i\cdot k}\cdot a_{k}\cdot b_{k+j}\cdot\left|k,k+j\right\rangle\Big)_{\mathsf{AD}}.

In particular, it holds that

|𝖤𝖯𝖱d⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|𝖤𝖯𝖱d⟩𝖢𝖣=1d⋅∑a,b=0d−1|𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅a,b⟩𝖠𝖣⊗|𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅−a,b⟩𝖡𝖢.\left|\mathsf{EPR}_{d}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}\otimes\left|\mathsf{EPR}_{d}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{D}}=\frac{1}{d}\cdot\sum_{a,b=0}^{d-1}\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{a,b}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{D}}\otimes\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{-a,b}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{C}}. (47)
Proof.

We begin by expanding the right-hand side.

1d⋅∑i,j|𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅i,j⟩𝖡𝖢⊗(∑kω−i⋅k⋅ak⋅bk+j⋅|k,k+j⟩)𝖠𝖣\displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\cdot\sum_{i,j}\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{i,j}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes\Big(\sum_{k}\omega^{-i\cdot k}\cdot a_{k}\cdot b_{k+j}\cdot\left|k,k+j\right\rangle\Big)_{\mathsf{AD}}
=\displaystyle={} 1d⋅∑i,j(1d⋅∑ℓ=0d−1ωi⋅ℓ|ℓ,ℓ+j⟩)⊗(∑kω−i⋅k⋅ak⋅bk+j⋅|k,k+j⟩)\displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\cdot\sum_{i,j}\Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\cdot\sum_{\ell=0}^{d-1}\omega^{i\cdot\ell}\left|\ell,\ell+j\right\rangle\Big)\otimes\Big(\sum_{k}\omega^{-i\cdot k}\cdot a_{k}\cdot b_{k+j}\cdot\left|k,k+j\right\rangle\Big)
=\displaystyle={} 1d⋅∑k,ℓ∑i,jωi⋅(ℓ−k)⋅ak⋅bk+j⋅|ℓ,ℓ+j⟩⊗|k,k+j⟩\displaystyle\frac{1}{d}\cdot\sum_{k,\ell}\sum_{i,j}\omega^{i\cdot(\ell-k)}\cdot a_{k}\cdot b_{k+j}\cdot\left|\ell,\ell+j\right\rangle\otimes\left|k,k+j\right\rangle
=\displaystyle={} ∑k∑jak⋅bk+j⋅|k,k+j⟩⊗|k,k+j⟩\displaystyle\sum_{k}\sum_{j}a_{k}\cdot b_{k+j}\cdot\left|k,k+j\right\rangle\otimes\left|k,k+j\right\rangle
=\displaystyle={} ∑k∑ℓak⋅bℓ⋅|k,ℓ⟩𝖠𝖢⊗|k,ℓ⟩𝖡𝖣\displaystyle\sum_{k}\sum_{\ell}a_{k}\cdot b_{\ell}\cdot\left|k,\ell\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AC}}\otimes\left|k,\ell\right\rangle_{\mathsf{BD}}
=\displaystyle={} |a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣.\displaystyle\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}.

This completes the proof. ∎

To understand equation (47) intuitively, suppose we are given |𝖤𝖯𝖱d⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|𝖤𝖯𝖱d⟩𝖢𝖣\left|\mathsf{EPR}_{d}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}\otimes\left|\mathsf{EPR}_{d}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{D}} and we measure subsystems 𝖡\mathsf{B} and 𝖢\mathsf{C} in the Bell basis. By Proposition D.4, if we receive outcome |𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅a,b⟩\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{a,b}\right\rangle, then the state in subsystems 𝖠\mathsf{A} and 𝖣\mathsf{D} collapses to |𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅−a,b⟩\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{-a,b}\right\rangle. Thus, we have exchanged a pair of maximally entangled states between subsystems 𝖠\mathsf{A} and 𝖡\mathsf{B} and between 𝖢\mathsf{C} and 𝖣\mathsf{D} with a pair between 𝖠\mathsf{A} and 𝖣\mathsf{D} and 𝖡\mathsf{B} and 𝖢\mathsf{C}. This is the protocol known as entanglement swapping.

In this work, we consider two means of generalizing the entanglement swapping protocol. First, we allow the starting state to be any bipartite state of the form |a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}, where |a⟩𝖠𝖡,|b⟩𝖢𝖣∈(ℂd)2\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}},\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}\in(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{2}, rather than just a tensor product of two EPR states. Second, we allow the measurement of the 𝖡\mathsf{B} and 𝖢\mathsf{C} subsystems to be any basis measurement |u1⟩,…,|ud2⟩\left|u_{1}\right\rangle,\ldots,\left|u_{d^{2}}\right\rangle in (ℂd)⊗2(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes 2}, rather than just the Bell basis measurement. More precisely, we consider the following protocol:

Definition D.5 (Entanglement swapping).

A general entanglement swapping protocol refers to the following procedure

  1. 1.

    Input: |ψ⟩=|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣\left|\psi\right\rangle=\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}} as in equation (46), and the unitary U=∑i∈[d2]|ui⟩​⟨i|U=\sum_{i\in[d^{2}]}|u_{i}\rangle\langle i| which specifies an orthonormal basis of (ℂd)⊗2(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes 2}.

  2. 2.

    Procedure: measure subsystems 𝖡𝖢\mathsf{BC} of |ψ⟩\left|\psi\right\rangle in the UU basis. Let pip_{i} be the probability of observing outcome ii, and ρi=(ρi)𝖠\rho_{i}=(\rho_{i})_{\mathsf{A}} be the reduced density matrix on subsystems 𝖠\mathsf{A} given this outcome.

  3. 3.

    Output: the pair (p,ρ)(p,\rho), where p=(p1,…,pd2)p=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{d^{2}}) and ρ=(ρ1,…,ρd2)\rho=(\rho_{1},\ldots,\rho_{d^{2}}). We write 𝝆\bm{\rho} for the random variable which is equal to ρi\rho_{i} with probability pip_{i}.

D.3 Reduction from shallow circuits to entanglement swapping

In this section, we focus on ground states that can be prepared with one-dimensional shallow quantum circuits. We will see that for such states, the study of the measurement-induced correlations and conditional independence reduces to a question about the performance of successive applications of the entanglement swapping protocol defined in Definition D.5.

We primarily consider the brickwork architecture of 1D quantum circuits, although our results apply more broadly to other geometrically-local circuits. In the brickwork architecture, as shown in Figure 3, the quantum circuit is constructed using alternating layers of two-quit gates. The odd-numbered layers consist of two-qudit gates acting on pairs of qudits (2​i,2​i+1)(2i,2i+1), while the even-numbered layers include gates acting on pairs of qudits (2​i−1,2​i)(2i-1,2i), where ii ranges from 11 to ⌊n−12⌋\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor.

Given a circuit of depth DD, we decompose the qudits and the gates as follows: Assume the number of qudits n=2​n′​(D−1)n=2n^{\prime}(D-1) for some integer n′≥1n^{\prime}\geq 1. Divide the set of qudits into contiguous subsets of size D−1D-1. We denote the odd subsets by 𝖫i\mathsf{L}_{i} and the even subsets by 𝖱i\mathsf{R}_{i} for i∈{1,…,n′}i\in\{1,\dots,n^{\prime}\}. The gates are partitioned into backward lightcones V1⊗⋯⊗Vn′V_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes V_{n^{\prime}} and forward lightcones U1⊗⋯⊗Un′−1U_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes U_{n^{\prime}-1} with triangular shapes as shown in Figure 3. The two-qudit gates in ViV_{i} act on the qudits in subsystems 𝖫i\mathsf{L}_{i} and 𝖱i\mathsf{R}_{i}, while the gates in UiU_{i} act on the qudits in subsystems 𝖱i\mathsf{R}_{i} and 𝖫i+1\mathsf{L}_{i+1}. Finally, we define the entangled state |a⟩𝖫i​𝖱i=Vi⋅|0⟩𝖫ii\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{i}\mathsf{R}_{i}}=V_{i}\cdot\left|0\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{i}\mathsf{}_{i}} for any pair of subsets (𝖫i,𝖱i)(\mathsf{L}_{i},\mathsf{R}_{i}).

Using this decomposition, we can now easily interpret the distribution obtained by measuring the output state of this one-dimensional shallow circuit using the entanglement swapping setup of Definition D.5. Initially multiple pairs of entangled states ⊗i=1n′|a⟩𝖫i,𝖱i\otimes_{i=1}^{n^{\prime}}\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{i},\mathsf{R}_{i}} are prepared. Subsequently, each pair of registers (𝖱i,𝖫i+1)(\mathsf{R}_{i},\mathsf{L}_{i+1}) is measured in the orthogonal basis {|uji⟩𝖱i​𝖫𝗂+𝟣}\{\left|u^{i}_{j}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{R}_{i}\mathsf{L_{i+1}}}\} specified by the unitary Ui=∑j=1d2​(D−1)|uji⟩​⟨j|U_{i}=\sum_{j=1}^{d^{2(D-1)}}|u^{i}_{j}\rangle\langle j|, starting from i=1i=1 and proceeding to the end of the circuit at i=n′−1i=n^{\prime}-1. Hence, to understand the nature of correlations that exist in the measurement distribution of a one-dimensional shallow circuit, we can study the states produced as the result of the corresponding entanglement swapping setup.

This reduction applies more generally to any state |ψ⟩\left|\psi\right\rangle with the zero-correlation length property. That is, if we can partition the qudits into contiguous groups 𝖳1,…,𝖳n′\mathsf{T}_{1},\dots,\mathsf{T}_{n^{\prime}} of size Θ⁡(D)\Theta(D), for some constant DD, such that

ρ𝖳i,𝖳j=ρ𝖳i⊗ρ𝖳j​ for any ​|i−j|>1.\displaystyle\rho_{\mathsf{T}_{i},\mathsf{T}_{j}}=\rho_{\mathsf{T}_{i}}\otimes\rho_{\mathsf{T}_{j}}\text{ for any }|i-j|>1.

We will later consider an example of entanglement swapping in such states with a zero correlation length in the context of one-dimensional sign-free states [32]. Using Uhlmann’s theorem, we see that there is an isometry UiU_{i} acting on each group of qudits 𝖳i\mathsf{T}_{i} that maps the Hilbert space into a tensor product of the form 𝖱i⊗𝖫i+1\mathsf{R}_{i}\otimes\mathsf{L}_{i+1} such that the resulting state is not entangled across subsystems 𝖱i\mathsf{R}_{i} and 𝖫i+1\mathsf{L}_{i+1}. By repeatedly applying such isometries UiU_{i} across the one-dimensional chain, we obtain a state of the form ⊗i|a⟩𝖫i​𝖱i\otimes_{i}\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{i}\mathsf{R}_{i}} similar to the decomposition we obtained earlier for the shallow quantum circuit. Depending on the Schmidt rank of the reduced state ρ𝖳1,…,𝖳i\rho_{\mathsf{T}_{1},\dots,\mathsf{T}_{i}}, the resulting tensor product space 𝖱i⊗𝖫i+1\mathsf{R}_{i}\otimes\mathsf{L}_{i+1} may have a smaller dimension than the original space and in general lacks the geometrically-local structure we observe in the reduction starting from shallow circuits.

Having obtained this reduction to the entanglement swapping protocol, we proceed with our objective of analyzing the correlations that arise from measuring interacting quantum systems on a one-dimensional chain. We consider contiguous subsets (𝖠,𝖡,𝖢)(\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B},\mathsf{C}) where 𝖠\mathsf{A} and 𝖢\mathsf{C} correspond respectively to 𝖫i\mathsf{L}_{i} and 𝖠j\mathsf{A}_{j} for some 1≤i<j≤n′1\leq i<j\leq n^{\prime}, and 𝖡\mathsf{B} corresponds to the qudits between 𝖫i\mathsf{L}_{i} and 𝖱j\mathsf{R}_{j}.

Given the zero-correlation length property, when the remaining qubits in [n]∖𝖠∪𝖡∪𝖢[n]\setminus\mathsf{A}\cup\mathsf{B}\cup\mathsf{C} are measured in the computational basis, only the state of subsystems (𝖫i,𝖱i)(\mathsf{L}_{i},\mathsf{R}_{i}) and (𝖫j,𝖱j)(\mathsf{L}_{j},\mathsf{R}_{j}) changes (from |a⟩𝖫i​𝖱i\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{i}\mathsf{R}_{i}} and |a⟩𝖫j​𝖱j\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{j}\mathsf{R}_{j}}), leaving the state of the remaining qudits in subset 𝖡∖𝖱i∪𝖫j\mathsf{B}\setminus\mathsf{R}_{i}\cup\mathsf{L}_{j} undisturbed. Therefore, in future sections, we often analyze the correlations between 𝖫1\mathsf{L}_{1} and 𝖱n′\mathsf{R}_{n^{\prime}} at the two ends of the chain, with the understanding that a similar analysis applies to subsystems 𝖫i\mathsf{L}_{i} and 𝖱j\mathsf{R}_{j} for 1<i<j<n′1<i<j<n^{\prime} when the states |a⟩𝖫i​𝖱𝗂\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{i}\mathsf{R_{i}}} and |a⟩𝖫j​𝖱j\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{j}\mathsf{R}_{j}} are possibly changed.

We study the correlations induced by entanglement swapping and in particular the notion of conditional independence in Definition II.1 using the classical conditional mutual information I(𝖠:𝖢|𝖡)I(\mathsf{A}:\mathsf{C}|\mathsf{B}) in the measurement distribution. We find it more convenient to analyze an upper bound on I(𝖠:𝖢|𝖡)I(\mathsf{A}:\mathsf{C}|\mathsf{B}) given in terms of the average von-Neumann entropy of the subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A}. It follows [52] from Holevo’s theorem that

I(𝖠:𝖢|𝖡)\displaystyle I(\mathsf{A}:\mathsf{C}|\mathsf{B}) :=𝔼𝒙𝖡DKL(p𝖠,𝖢|𝒙𝖡∥p𝖠|𝒙𝖡⊗p𝖡|𝒙𝖡)\displaystyle:=\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}D_{\text{KL}}(p_{{\mathsf{A}},{\mathsf{C}}|\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}\parallel p_{{\mathsf{A}}|\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}\otimes p_{{\mathsf{B}}|\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}})
≤𝔼𝒙𝖡​S​(ρ𝖠|𝒙𝖡)\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}S(\rho_{\mathsf{A}|{\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}}) (48)

Therefore, to prove the conditional independence property (4), it suffices to find an upper bound on the average entropy of the post-measurement state 𝔼𝒙𝖡​S​(ρ𝖠|𝒙𝖡)\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}S(\rho_{\mathsf{A}|{\bm{x}_{\mathsf{B}}}}).

D.4 Optimal entanglement swapping for qubits

We start with when entanglement swapping measurement is performed on qubits. Our main result is a tight upper bound on the expected entropy 𝔼​S​(𝝆𝖠)\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}) of the state 𝝆𝖠\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}} generated in this process.

Prior to stating this result, we gather some definitions and notations. We let ℋ𝖠𝖡𝖢𝖣\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{ABCD}} denote a Hilbert space containing four subsystems 𝖠\mathsf{A}, 𝖡\mathsf{B}, 𝖢\mathsf{C}, and 𝖣\mathsf{D} of dimension d=2d=2 each. Let |u1⟩,|u2⟩,|u3⟩,|u4⟩\left|u_{1}\right\rangle,\left|u_{2}\right\rangle,\left|u_{3}\right\rangle,\left|u_{4}\right\rangle be an orthonormal basis of ℋ𝖡𝖢\mathcal{H}_{\mathsf{BC}}, where

|ui⟩𝖡𝖢=u00i|00⟩+u01i|01⟩+u10i|10⟩+u11i|11⟩.\left|u_{i}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{BC}}=u_{00}^{i}\left|00\right\rangle+u_{01}^{i}\left|01\right\rangle+u_{10}^{i}\left|10\right\rangle+u_{11}^{i}\left|11\right\rangle.

The (unnormalized) post-measurement state after receiving outcome ii is given by

|ψi⟩𝖠𝖣\displaystyle\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}} =⟨ui|𝖡𝖢⋅|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣\displaystyle=\left\langle u_{i}\right|_{\mathsf{BC}}\cdot\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}
=(∑x∈{0,1}2(uxi)†⟨x|𝖡𝖢)⋅(∑y∈{0,1}2ay1by2|y1y1⟩𝖠𝖡|y2y2⟩𝖢𝖣)=∑x∈{0,1}2(uxi)†ax1bx2⋅|x⟩.\displaystyle=\Bigg(\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{2}}(u^{i}_{x})^{\dagger}\left\langle x\right|_{\mathsf{BC}}\Bigg)\cdot\Bigg(\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^{2}}a_{y_{1}}b_{y_{2}}\left|y_{1}y_{1}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\left|y_{2}y_{2}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}\Bigg)=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{2}}(u_{x}^{i})^{\dagger}a_{x_{1}}b_{x_{2}}\cdot\left|x\right\rangle. (49)

The probability of receiving outcome ii is

pi=⟨ψi|ψi⟩=∑x∈{0,1}2|uxi|2⋅|ax1|2​|bx2|2.p_{i}=\left\langle\psi_{i}\middle|\psi_{i}\right\rangle=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{2}}|u_{x}^{i}|^{2}\cdot|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x_{2}}|^{2}. (50)

Hence, the normalized post-measurement state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} is

ρ𝖠i=1pi⋅(|ψi⟩⟨ψi|)𝖠.\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}=\frac{1}{p_{i}}\cdot(\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle\left\langle\psi_{i}\right|)_{\mathsf{A}}. (51)

The main result of this section is stated as follows.

Theorem D.6 (Upper bound on binary entanglement swapping).

Following an entanglement swapping measurement in an arbitrary basis UU on the state |ψ⟩\left|\psi\right\rangle defined by

|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣=(a0|00⟩+a1|11⟩)⊗(b0|00⟩+b1|11⟩),\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}=\Big(a_{0}\left|00\right\rangle+a_{1}\left|11\right\rangle\Big)\otimes\Big(b_{0}\left|00\right\rangle+b_{1}\left|11\right\rangle\Big), (52)

the average entropy S⁡(𝛒𝖠)S(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}) of the output state is bounded by

𝔼​S​(𝝆𝖠)≤p0⋅S⁡(ρ0)+p1⋅S⁡(ρ1)\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}})\leq p_{0}\cdot S(\rho_{0})+p_{1}\cdot S(\rho_{1}) (53)

where p0=|a0|2​|b0|2+|a1|2​|b1|2p_{0}=|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}+|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}, p1=|a0|2​|b1|2+|a1|2​|b0|2p_{1}=|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}+|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}, and we have

ρ𝖠0=1p0⋅(|a0|2​|b0|200|a1|2​|b1|2),ρ𝖠1=1p1⋅(|a0|2​|b1|200|a1|2​|b0|2).\displaystyle\rho^{0}_{\mathsf{A}}=\frac{1}{p_{0}}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}&0\\ 0&|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}\end{pmatrix},\quad\rho^{1}_{\mathsf{A}}=\frac{1}{p_{1}}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}&0\\ 0&|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}\end{pmatrix}.

Moreover, the equality is achieved when the measurement is performed in the Bell basis as in Definition D.3.

To give a detailed proof of Theorem D.6, we consider the experiment of measuring |a⟩⊗|b⟩\left|a\right\rangle\otimes\left|b\right\rangle in the basis |x⟩𝖠𝖣⊗|ui⟩𝖡𝖢\left|x\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}}\otimes\left|u_{i}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{BC}} over x∈{0,1}2x\in\{0,1\}^{2} and i∈{1,2,3,4}i\in\{1,2,3,4\}. If we do so, then by Equation (49) we receive outcome (x,i)(x,i) with probability |uxi|2⋅|ax1|2​|bx2|2|u^{i}_{x}|^{2}\cdot|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x_{2}}|^{2}. This motivates studying the following random variable.

Definition D.7 (Measurement outcome random variable).

We define (𝐗,𝐈)(\bm{X},\bm{I}) to be the random variable which is equal to (x,i)(x,i) with probability |uxi|2⋅|ax1|2​|bx2|2|u^{i}_{x}|^{2}\cdot|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x_{2}}|^{2}.

One property we will need of this random variable is whether the string 𝑿\bm{X} is even or odd. This is formalized in the following definition.

Definition D.8.

We write odd⁡(𝐗)\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X}) for the {0,1}\{0,1\}-valued random variable defined as

odd⁡(𝑿):=𝑿1+𝑿2(mod2).\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X}):=\bm{X}_{1}+\bm{X}_{2}\pmod{2}.

Equivalently, odd⁡(𝐗)=1\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})=1 when 𝐗1=𝐗2\bm{X}_{1}=\bm{X}_{2} and 00 otherwise.

Our key technical lemma relates the von Neumann entropy of the state ρi\rho_{i} with the Shannon entropy of the random variable (𝑿,𝑰)(\bm{X},\bm{I}). It is stated as follows.

Lemma D.9.

For each i∈{1,2,3,4}i\in\{1,2,3,4\},

S⁡(ρ𝖠i)≤H⁡(𝑿∣odd⁡(𝑿),𝑰=i).S(\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}})\leq H(\bm{X}\mid\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X}),\bm{I}=i). (54)

Prior to proving Lemma D.9, we show how it can be used to complete the proof of Theorem D.6.

Proof of Theorem D.6.

We first specialize to the case that the entanglement swapping measurement is performed in the Bell basis. Proposition D.4 for qubits d=2d=2, implies that

|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣=12⋅∑i,j∈{0,1}|𝖡𝖾𝗅𝗅i,j⟩𝖡𝖢⊗(a0⋅bj⋅|0,j⟩+(−1)i⋅a1⋅b1+j⋅|1,1+j⟩)𝖠𝖣,\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\sum_{i,j\in\{0,1\}}\left|\mathsf{Bell}_{i,j}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes\Big(a_{0}\cdot b_{j}\cdot\left|0,j\right\rangle+(-1)^{i}\cdot a_{1}\cdot b_{1+j}\cdot\left|1,1+j\right\rangle\Big)_{\mathsf{AD}},

and that 𝝆\bm{\rho} is distributed as follows:

ρ𝖠0=1p0⋅(|a0|2​|b0|200|a1|2​|b1|2),\displaystyle\rho^{0}_{\mathsf{A}}=\frac{1}{p_{0}}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}&0\\ 0&|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}\end{pmatrix}, with probability p0=|a0|2​|b0|2+|a1|2​|b1|2,\displaystyle\qquad\text{with probability $p_{0}=|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}+|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}$},
ρ𝖠1=1p1⋅(|a0|2​|b1|200|a1|2​|b0|2),\displaystyle\rho^{1}_{\mathsf{A}}=\frac{1}{p_{1}}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}&0\\ 0&|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}\end{pmatrix}, with probability p1=|a0|2​|b1|2+|a1|2​|b0|2.\displaystyle\qquad\text{with probability $p_{1}=|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}+|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}$}. (55)

Hence, when measured in the Bell basis, we have 𝑬⁡(𝝆𝖠)=p0⋅S⁡(ρ0)+p1⋅S⁡(ρ1)\bm{E}(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}})=p_{0}\cdot S(\rho_{0})+p_{1}\cdot S(\rho_{1}). We next show that in an arbitrary basis, it holds that 𝑬⁡(𝝆𝖠)≤p0⋅S⁡(ρ𝖠0)+p1⋅S⁡(ρ𝖠1)\bm{E}(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}})\leq p_{0}\cdot S(\rho^{0}_{\mathsf{A}})+p_{1}\cdot S(\rho^{1}_{\mathsf{A}}). This follows from

∑i=14pi​S​(ρ𝖠i)\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{4}p_{i}S(\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}) =∑i=14Pr[𝑰=i]⋅S(ρ𝖠i)\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{4}\mathrm{Pr}[\bm{I}=i]\cdot S(\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}) (by definition of 𝑰\bm{I})
≤∑i=14Pr[𝑰=i]⋅H(𝑿∣odd(𝑿),𝑰=i)\displaystyle\leq\sum_{i=1}^{4}\mathrm{Pr}[\bm{I}=i]\cdot H(\bm{X}\mid\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X}),\bm{I}=i) (by Lemma D.9)
=H⁡(𝑿∣odd⁡(𝑿),𝑰)\displaystyle=H(\bm{X}\mid\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X}),\bm{I})
≤H⁡(𝑿∣odd⁡(𝑿))\displaystyle\leq H(\bm{X}\mid\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})) (because conditioning reduces entropy)
=H⁡(𝑿)−H⁡(odd⁡(𝑿)).\displaystyle=H(\bm{X})-H(\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})).

But

H⁡(𝑿)=H⁡(|a0|2,|a1|2)+H⁡(|b0|2,|b1|2)H(\bm{X})=H(|a_{0}|^{2},|a_{1}|^{2})+H(|b_{0}|^{2},|b_{1}|^{2})

and

H⁡(odd⁡(𝑿))=H⁡(|a0|2​|b0|2+|a1|2​|b1|2,|a0|2​|b1|2+|a1|2​|b0|2).H(\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X}))=H(|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}+|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2},|a_{0}|^{2}|b_{1}|^{2}+|a_{1}|^{2}|b_{0}|^{2}).

Hence, a direct calculation shows that

H⁡(𝑿)−H⁡(odd⁡(𝑿))=p0⋅S⁡(ρ𝖠0)+p1⋅S⁡(ρ𝖠1),H(\bm{X})-H(\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X}))=p_{0}\cdot S(\rho^{0}_{\mathsf{A}})+p_{1}\cdot S(\rho^{1}_{\mathsf{A}}),

where probabilities p0p_{0} and p1p_{1}, and the states ρ0\rho_{0} and ρ1\rho_{1} are given by (55). This leads to the claimed bound in (53) and completes the proof of Theorem D.6. ∎

Finally, we state the proof of Lemma D.9.

Proof of Lemma D.9.

Let |ϕ⟩𝖠𝖣=a|00⟩+b|11⟩+c|01⟩+d|10⟩\left|\phi\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}}=a\left|00\right\rangle+b\left|11\right\rangle+c\left|01\right\rangle+d\left|10\right\rangle be a normalized bipartite state. This state may correspond to any of the post-measurement states |ψi⟩𝖠𝖣\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}} for i∈{1,2,3,4}i\in\{1,2,3,4\}. The reduced state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} is given by

ρ=(|a|2+|c|2a​d∗+b∗​ca∗​d+b​c∗|b|2+|d|2).\displaystyle\rho=\begin{pmatrix}|a|^{2}+|c|^{2}&ad^{*}+b^{*}c\\ a^{*}d+bc^{*}&|b|^{2}+|d|^{2}\end{pmatrix}.

The following projective measurements correspond to obtaining odd⁡(𝑿)=0\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})=0 and odd⁡(𝑿)=1\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})=1:

odd⁡(𝑿)=0,Π0=|00⟩​⟨00|+|11⟩​⟨11|,\displaystyle\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})=0,\quad\Pi_{0}=|00\rangle\langle 00|+|11\rangle\langle 11|,\quad
odd⁡(𝑿)=1,Π1=|01⟩​⟨01|+|10⟩​⟨10|.\displaystyle\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})=1,\quad\Pi_{1}=|01\rangle\langle 01|+|10\rangle\langle 10|.

For each of these two measurements, the reduced post-measurement state and its measurement probability is

odd(𝑿)=0:σ0=(|a|2|a|2+|b|200|b|2|a|2+|b|2),with probabilityq0=|a|2+|b|2,\displaystyle\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})=0:\quad\sigma_{0}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{|a|^{2}}{|a|^{2}+|b|^{2}}&0\\ 0&\frac{|b|^{2}}{|a|^{2}+|b|^{2}}\end{pmatrix},\quad\textit{with probability}\quad q_{0}=|a|^{2}+|b|^{2},
odd(𝑿)=1:σ1=(|c|2|c|2+|d|200|d|2|c|2+|d|2),with probability.q1=|c|2+|d|2.\displaystyle\mathrm{odd}(\bm{X})=1:\quad\sigma_{1}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{|c|^{2}}{|c|^{2}+|d|^{2}}&0\\ 0&\frac{|d|^{2}}{|c|^{2}+|d|^{2}}\end{pmatrix},\quad\textit{with probability.}\quad q_{1}=|c|^{2}+|d|^{2}. (56)

Our goal is to prove the bound (54) which in this setup is equivalent to proving

S⁡(ρ)≤q0⋅S⁡(σ0)+q1⋅S⁡(σ1).\displaystyle S(\rho)\leq q_{0}\cdot S(\sigma_{0})+q_{1}\cdot S(\sigma_{1}). (57)

We prove this by interpreting the entropy term S⁡(ρ)S(\rho) as the entanglement of formation of a two-qubit mixed state τ𝖠𝖣\tau_{\mathsf{AD}} and drawing on Definition D.2. Consider the following pair of pure states

|ϕ0⟩𝖠𝖣=1|a|2+|b|2(a|00⟩+b|11⟩),|ϕ1⟩𝖠𝖣=1|c|2+|d|2(c|01⟩+d|10⟩),\left|\phi_{0}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|a|^{2}+|b|^{2}}}\left(a\left|00\right\rangle+b\left|11\right\rangle\right),\quad\left|\phi_{1}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|c|^{2}+|d|^{2}}}\left(c\left|01\right\rangle+d\left|10\right\rangle\right),

and their mixture τ𝖠𝖣\tau_{\mathsf{AD}} given by

τ𝖠𝖣=p0⋅|ϕ0⟩​⟨ϕ0|𝖠𝖣+p1⋅|ϕ1⟩​⟨ϕ1|𝖠𝖣=(|a|200a​b∗0|c|2c​d∗00c∗​d|d|20a∗​b00|b|2),\displaystyle\tau_{\mathsf{AD}}=p_{0}\cdot|\phi_{0}\rangle\langle\phi_{0}|_{\mathsf{AD}}+p_{1}\cdot|\phi_{1}\rangle\langle\phi_{1}|_{\mathsf{AD}}=\begin{pmatrix}|a|^{2}&0&0&ab^{*}\\ 0&|c|^{2}&cd^{*}&0\\ 0&c^{*}d&|d|^{2}&0\\ a^{*}b&0&0&|b|^{2}\end{pmatrix}, (58)

where as before q0=|a|2+|b|2q_{0}=|a|^{2}+|b|^{2} and q1=|c|2+|d|2q_{1}=|c|^{2}+|d|^{2}. The states σ0\sigma_{0} and σ1\sigma_{1} in (56) correspond to the reduced state of |ϕ1⟩𝖠𝖣\left|\phi_{1}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}} and |ϕ2⟩𝖠𝖣\left|\phi_{2}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}} on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A}. Hence, following Definition D.2, the entanglement of formation EF​(τ𝖠𝖡)E_{F}(\tau_{\mathsf{AB}}) satisfies

EF​(τ𝖠𝖡)≤q0⋅S⁡(σ0)+q1⋅S⁡(σ1).\displaystyle E_{F}(\tau_{\mathsf{AB}})\leq q_{0}\cdot S(\sigma_{0})+q_{1}\cdot S(\sigma_{1}). (59)

Using Fact D.3, the entanglement of formation EF​(τ𝖠𝖡)E_{F}(\tau_{\mathsf{AB}}) can be explicitly calculated as

EF​(τ𝖠𝖡)=h⁡(1+1−C​(τ𝖠𝖣)22),\displaystyle E_{F}(\tau_{\mathsf{AB}})=h\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{1-C(\tau_{\mathsf{AD}})^{2}}}{2}\right), (60)

where the concurrence C⁡(τ𝖠𝖣)C(\tau_{\mathsf{AD}}) is given by C⁡(τ𝖠𝖣)=2⋅|a​b−c​d|C(\tau_{\mathsf{AD}})=2\cdot|ab-cd| as per Fact D.1. We now claim that the entropy S⁡(ρ)S(\rho) in (57) is equal to EF​(τ𝖠𝖡)E_{F}(\tau_{\mathsf{AB}}). This follows from the fact that

S⁡(ρ)=h⁡(1+1−C​(ϕ𝖠𝖣)22)\displaystyle S(\rho)=h\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{1-C(\phi_{\mathsf{AD}})^{2}}}{2}\right) (61)

according to Fact D.2, and that C⁡(ϕ𝖠𝖣)=2⋅|a​b−c​d|C(\phi_{\mathsf{AD}})=2\cdot|ab-cd| using Fact D.1. Going back to (59), we see that S⁡(ρ)≤q0⋅S⁡(σ0)+q1⋅S⁡(σ1)S(\rho)\leq q_{0}\cdot S(\sigma_{0})+q_{1}\cdot S(\sigma_{1}), which completes the proof. ∎

Next, we give an alternative looser upper bound on the average entropy 𝔼​S​(𝝆𝖠)\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}) again by using the notion of concurrence. The usefulness of this bound will become clear in the next section where we consider a contiguous series of entanglement swapping measurements performed on a chain of two-qubit entangled pairs. A similar analysis for a pair of qubits has been considered before in [59, 70] in the context of localizable entanglement.

We begin with a known general upper bound on the entropy S⁡(ρ)S(\rho) in terms of concurrence C⁡(ρ)C(\rho).

Theorem D.10 (Entropy bound in terms of concurrence, cf. [33]).

Let ρ\rho be a rank dd state. The following upper bound on the von Neumann entropy of ρ\rho holds:

S⁡(ρ)≤cd⋅C⁡(ρ).\displaystyle S(\rho)\leq c_{d}\cdot C(\rho). (62)

Here cd=log⁡(d)⋅d2​(d−1)c_{d}=\log(d)\cdot\sqrt{\frac{d}{2(d-1)}} and the concurrence is given by C⁡(ρ)=2⋅(tr⁡(ρ)2−tr⁡(ρ2))C(\rho)=\sqrt{2\cdot(\operatorname{tr}(\rho)^{2}-\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2}))}. In particular, in the case of a qubit d=2d=2, we can bound the entropy S⁡(ρ)S(\rho) of a qubit by its concurrence C⁡(ρ)C(\rho) via

S⁡(ρ)≤C⁡(ρ)for qubits.\displaystyle S(\rho)\leq C(\rho)\quad\text{for qubits}. (63)

By applying the bound (63), we prove the following result.

Proposition D.11 (Alternative upper bound on average entropy ).

Following an entanglement swapping measurement on qubit states |a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣=(a0|00⟩+a1|11⟩)⊗(b0|00⟩+b1|11⟩)\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}=\Big(a_{0}\left|00\right\rangle+a_{1}\left|11\right\rangle\Big)\otimes\Big(b_{0}\left|00\right\rangle+b_{1}\left|11\right\rangle\Big) as in Definition D.5, the average entropy 𝔼​S​(𝛒𝖠)\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}) and concurrence 𝔼​C​(𝛒𝖠)\mathbb{E\/}C(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}) of the state ρ𝖠\rho_{\mathsf{A}} satisfy

𝔼​S​(𝝆𝖠)≤𝔼​C​(𝝆𝖠)≤4⋅|a0​a1|⋅|b0​b1|.\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}})\leq\mathbb{E\/}C(\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}})\leq 4\cdot|a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot|b_{0}b_{1}|. (64)

The proof of this proposition entails finding the concurrence of the post-measurement states which we detail first. Using our notation in equations (49)-(51), the un-normalized state on subsystems 𝖠𝖣\mathsf{AD} after measuring subsystems 𝖡𝖢\mathsf{BC} is given by

|ψi⟩𝖠𝖣=∑x∈{0,1}2(uxi)†ax1bx2⋅|x⟩,\displaystyle\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AD}}=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{2}}(u_{x}^{i})^{\dagger}a_{x_{1}}b_{x_{2}}\cdot\left|x\right\rangle, (65)

and the corresponding reduced state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} is denoted by ρ~𝖠i=pi⋅ρ𝖠i\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}=p_{i}\cdot\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}. Given this and the definition of concurrence in equation (38), we see that C⁡(ρ~𝖠i)=pi⋅C⁡(ρi)C(\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}})=p_{i}\cdot C(\rho_{i}), and therefore, the average concurrence satisfies ∑ipi⋅C⁡(ρ𝖠i)=∑iC⁡(ρ~𝖠i)\sum_{i}p_{i}\cdot C(\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}})=\sum_{i}C(\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}).

This expression for this concurrence in the general case of qudits is stated in the next lemma.

Lemma D.12 (Post-measurement concurrence).

The concurrence of the post-measurement state C⁡(ρ~𝖠i)C(\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}) is given by

C⁡(ρ~𝖠i)=(∑x1<x1′,x2<x2′|ux1​x2i​ux1′​x2′i−ux1​x2′i​ux1′​x2i|2​|ax1|2​|ax1′|2​|bx2|2​|bx2′|2)1/2,\displaystyle C(\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}})=\left(\sum_{x_{1}<x^{\prime}_{1},x_{2}<x^{\prime}_{2}}|u^{i}_{x_{1}x_{2}}u^{i}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}-u^{i}_{x_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}u^{i}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x_{2}}|^{2}|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|a_{x^{\prime}_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x_{2}}|^{2}|b_{x^{\prime}_{2}}|^{2}\right)^{1/2}, (66)
Proof.

A direct calculation shows that

tr⁡[ρ~𝖠i]=∑x1,x1′∈{0,1}|ux1​x1′i|2​|ax1|2​|bx1′|2\displaystyle\operatorname{tr}[\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}]=\sum_{x_{1},x^{\prime}_{1}\in\{0,1\}}|u^{i}_{x_{1}x^{\prime}_{1}}|^{2}|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x^{\prime}_{1}}|^{2}

and

tr[(ρ~𝖠i)2]=∑x,x′∈{0,1}2ux1​x2iux1′​x2i∗ux1′​x2′iux1​x2′i∗|ax1|2|bx2|2|ax1′|2|bx2′|2.\displaystyle\operatorname{tr}[(\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}})^{2}]=\sum_{x,x^{\prime}\in\{0,1\}^{2}}u^{i}_{x_{1}x_{2}}u^{i*}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x_{2}}u^{i}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}u^{i*}_{x_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x_{2}}|^{2}|a_{x^{\prime}_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x^{\prime}_{2}}|^{2}.

Hence,

C​(ρ~𝖠i)2\displaystyle C(\tilde{\rho}^{i}_{\mathsf{A}})^{2} =2⋅∑x1,x2,x1′,x2′(|ux1​x2i|2|ux1′,x2′i|2−ux1,x2iux1′​x2i∗ux1′​x2′iux1​x2′i∗)⋅|ax1|2|ax1′|2|bx2|2|bx2′|2\displaystyle=2\cdot\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},x^{\prime}_{1},x^{\prime}_{2}}\left(|u^{i}_{x_{1}x_{2}}|^{2}|u^{i}_{x^{\prime}_{1},x^{\prime}_{2}}|^{2}-u^{i}_{x_{1},x_{2}}u^{i*}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x_{2}}u^{i}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}u^{i*}_{x_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}\right)\cdot|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|a_{x^{\prime}_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x_{2}}|^{2}|b_{x^{\prime}_{2}}|^{2}
=4⋅∑x1<x1′,x2<x2′|ux1​x2i​ux1′​x2′i−ux1​x2′i​ux1′​x2i|2​|ax1|2​|ax1′|2​|bx2|2​|bx2′|2.\displaystyle=4\cdot\sum_{x_{1}<x^{\prime}_{1},x_{2}<x^{\prime}_{2}}|u^{i}_{x_{1}x_{2}}u^{i}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}-u^{i}_{x_{1}x^{\prime}_{2}}u^{i}_{x^{\prime}_{1}x_{2}}|^{2}|a_{x_{1}}|^{2}|a_{x^{\prime}_{1}}|^{2}|b_{x_{2}}|^{2}|b_{x^{\prime}_{2}}|^{2}. (67)

∎

Next we show how in the case of qubits (d=2d=2), the bound (64) on the average entropy can be deduced from (66):

Proof of Proposition D.11.

In this case, the bounds (63) and (66) imply

∑i=14pi⋅S⁡(ρ𝖠i)≤∑i=14pi⋅C⁡(ρ𝖠i)\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{4}p_{i}\cdot S(\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}})\leq\sum_{i=1}^{4}p_{i}\cdot C(\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}) ≤2⋅|a0​a1|⋅|b0​b1|⋅∑i=14|u00i​u11i−u10i​u01i|\displaystyle\leq 2\cdot|a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot|b_{0}b_{1}|\cdot\sum_{i=1}^{4}|u^{i}_{00}u^{i}_{11}-u^{i}_{10}u^{i}_{01}| (68)
≤|a0​a1|⋅|b0|​|b1|⋅∑i=14((u00i)2+(u11i)2+(u01i)2+(u10i)2)\displaystyle\leq|a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot|b_{0}||b_{1}|\cdot\sum_{i=1}^{4}\left((u_{00}^{i})^{2}+(u_{11}^{i})^{2}+(u_{01}^{i})^{2}+(u_{10}^{i})^{2}\right)
=4⋅|a0​a1|⋅|b0​b1|.\displaystyle=4\cdot|a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot|b_{0}b_{1}|.

We note that the second inequality is tight when subsystems 𝖢𝖣\mathsf{CD} are measured in the Bell basis. ∎

D.5 Cluster state

We next apply the previous lemma along a one-dimensional chain to show that the conditional correlations between the two end points of the chain decay exponentially with the length of the chain.

Theorem D.13 (Decay of CMI for a chain of qubits).

Consider the state ⊗k=1n|a⟩𝖫k​𝖱k\otimes_{k=1}^{n}\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{k}\mathsf{R}_{k}} where |a⟩𝖫k​𝖱k=a00|00⟩𝖫k​𝖱k+a11|11⟩𝖫k​𝖱k\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{k}\mathsf{R}_{k}}=a_{00}\left|00\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{k}\mathsf{R}_{k}}+a_{11}\left|11\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{k}\mathsf{R}_{k}}. Suppose we measure each pair of registers (𝖱j,𝖫j+1)(\mathsf{R}_{j},\mathsf{L}_{j+1}) for j∈[n−1]j\in[n-1] in an arbitrary four dimensional orthonormal basis. Let 𝛒1\bm{\rho}_{1} be the post-measurement state on qubit 𝖫1\mathsf{L}_{1}. It holds that

𝔼​S​(𝝆1)≤|2​a0​a1|n.\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{1})\leq|2a_{0}a_{1}|^{n}. (69)

Since a0​a1≤12a_{0}a_{1}\leq\frac{1}{2}, this implies an exponentially decaying bound 𝔼​S​(𝛒1)≤e−Ω⁡(n)\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{1})\leq e^{-\Omega(n)} in terms of nn unless a0=a1=1/2a_{0}=a_{1}=1/\sqrt{2}, i.e. the state |a⟩\left|a\right\rangle is a maximally entangled state.

Proof.

We assume that the joint measurements on registers (𝖱j,𝖫j+1)(\mathsf{R}_{j},\mathsf{L}_{j+1}) are performed sequentially starting from (𝖱1,𝖫2)(\mathsf{R}_{1},\mathsf{L}_{2}). The measurement outcomes in each of these measurements are denoted by random variables 𝒊1,…,𝒊n−1∈{0,1}2\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1}\in\{0,1\}^{2}. Given these outcomes, we let 𝝆1(𝒊1​…,𝒊k)\bm{\rho}^{(\bm{i}_{1}\,\dots,\bm{i}_{k})}_{1} be the post-measurement state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} upon the first kk measurements. Our goal is to upper bound 𝔼𝒊1,…,𝒊n−1​S​(𝝆1(𝒊1​…,𝒊n−1))\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1}}S(\bm{\rho}_{1}^{(\bm{i}_{1}\,\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1})}). This can be achieved by finding an upper bound on the expected concurrence 𝔼𝒊1,…,𝒊n−1​C​(𝝆1(𝒊1​…,𝒊n−1))\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1}}C(\bm{\rho}^{(\bm{i}_{1}\,\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1})}_{1}), and applying the inequality (63) in Theorem D.10.

Consider the last measurement performed on subsystems 𝖱𝗇−𝟣​𝖫𝗇\mathsf{R_{n-1}L_{n}}, and suppose the previous measurements have returned the values i1,…,in−2i_{1},\dots,i_{n-2} with a corresponding post-measurement state ρ(i1,…,in−2)\rho^{(i_{1},\dots,i_{n-2})} on subsystems 𝖫𝟣\mathsf{L_{1}}. Using (64), we have that

𝔼𝒊n−1​C​(𝝆1(i1,…,in−2,𝒊n−1))≤2⋅|a0​a1|⋅C⁡(ρ1(i1,…,in−2)).\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}_{n-1}}C(\bm{\rho}_{1}^{(i_{1},\dots,i_{n-2},\bm{i}_{n-1})})\leq 2\cdot|a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot C(\rho_{1}^{(i_{1},\dots,i_{n-2})}). (70)

This implies the following bound on the expected concurrence over the measurement outcomes on subsystems 𝖱n−2​𝖫n−1\mathsf{R}_{n-2}\mathsf{L}_{n-1}

𝔼𝒊n−2,𝒊n−1​C​(𝝆1(i1,…,in−2,𝒊n−1))\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}_{n-2},\bm{i}_{n-1}}C(\bm{\rho}_{1}^{(i_{1},\dots,i_{n-2},\bm{i}_{n-1})}) ≤|2​a0​a1|⋅𝔼𝒊n−2​C​(𝝆1(i1,…,𝒊n−2))\displaystyle\leq|2a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}_{n-2}}C(\bm{\rho}_{1}^{(i_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-2})})
≤|2​a0​a1|2⋅C⁡(ρ1(i1,…,in−3)),\displaystyle\leq|2a_{0}a_{1}|^{2}\cdot C(\rho_{1}^{(i_{1},\dots,i_{n-3})}), (71)

where the last inequality via another application of (64). Iterating in this manner over all the n−1n-1 measurements yields the claimed bound (69). ∎

We now apply this bound to the rotated 1D cluster state which is the ground state of the Hamiltonian in (9). In the standard basis, the rotated cluster state is the ground state of H=−∑k=2n−1Xk−1ZkXk+1−Z1X2−Xn−1Xn−Xn−2Zn−1Zn.H=-\sum_{k=2}^{n-1}X_{k-1}Z_{k}X_{k+1}-Z_{1}X_{2}-X_{n-1}X_{n}-X_{n-2}Z_{n-1}Z_{n}. This state can be prepared by first producing a series of EPR pairs on qubits i,i+1i,i+1 for i∈[n−1]i\in[n-1]. Then a Bell-basis unitary is applied on qubits 2​i,2​i+12i,2i+1 for i=n/2−1i=n/2-1.

Hence, due to the measurement-induced entanglement, the measurement distribution in the ZZ-basis exhibits long-range conditional correlations. In contrast, measuring in the XX-basis results in a uniform distribution that lacks any correlations. More generally, measuring in a rotated basis induces an exponential decay of correlations, as formally stated in the following corollary:

Corollary D.1 (Decay of CMI in cluster state, restatement of Theorem III.1).

Consider the rotated nn-qubit cluster state given by the circuit in Figure 6 for an even nn. This circuit prepares n/2n/2 EPR pairs followed by a Bell basis rotation. We then apply a yy-rotation 11 1 This is the same as changing XX and ZZ Pauli operators in the cluster state Hamiltonian to X→cos⁡(2​θ)⋅X−sin⁡(2​θ)⋅Z,Z→cos⁡(2​θ)⋅Z+sin⁡(2​θ)⋅XX\rightarrow\cos(2\theta)\cdot X-\sin(2\theta)\cdot Z,\quad Z\rightarrow\cos(2\theta)\cdot Z+\sin(2\theta)\cdot X. given by

Ry​(θ)=(cos⁡(θ/2)sin⁡(θ/2)−sin⁡(θ/2)cos⁡(θ/2))=cos⁡(θ/2)⋅𝟙+i​sin⁡(θ/2)⋅Y,θ∈[0,π/2]\displaystyle R_{y}(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&&\sin(\theta/2)\\ -\sin(\theta/2)&&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}=\cos(\theta/2)\cdot\mathds{1}+i\sin(\theta/2)\cdot Y,\quad\quad\theta\in[0,\pi/2] (72)

to each qubit and proceed to measure all but the first and the last qubits in the standard ZZ basis. The post-measurement state 𝛒1\bm{\rho}_{1} on the first qubit satisfies

𝔼​S​(𝝆1)≤cos⁡(θ)n−2.\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}S(\bm{\rho}_{1})\leq\cos(\theta)^{n-2}. (73)
Proof.

We first bound the expected entropy after one application of the entanglement swapping measurement as in (68). One can directly calculate that in the yy-rotated basis, we have

|u00i​u11i−u10i​u01i|=12⋅cos⁡(θ)2.\displaystyle|u^{i}_{00}u^{i}_{11}-u^{i}_{10}u^{i}_{01}|=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\cos(\theta)^{2}.

Applying this to (68) yields

∑i=14pi​S​(ρ1i)≤∑i=14pi​C​(ρ1i)\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{4}p_{i}S(\rho^{i}_{1})\leq\sum_{i=1}^{4}p_{i}C(\rho^{i}_{1}) ≤2⋅|a0​a1|⋅|b0​b1|⋅∑i=14|u00i​u11i−u10i​u01i|\displaystyle\leq 2\cdot|a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot|b_{0}b_{1}|\cdot\sum_{i=1}^{4}|u^{i}_{00}u^{i}_{11}-u^{i}_{10}u^{i}_{01}|
=cos⁡(θ)2⋅2​|a0​a1|⋅2​|b0​b1|\displaystyle=\cos(\theta)^{2}\cdot 2|a_{0}a_{1}|\cdot 2|b_{0}b_{1}|

The remainder of the proof follows similar to that of Theorem D.13 (note the different number of qubits used in Theorem D.13). In particular, the cluster state satisfies a0=a1=12a_{0}=a_{1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, and hence, the bound in equation (70) changes to

𝔼𝒊n−1​C​(𝝆1(i1,…,in−2,𝒊n−1))≤cos⁡(θ)2⋅C⁡(ρ1(i1,…,in−2)).\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}_{n-1}}C(\bm{\rho}_{1}^{(i_{1},\dots,i_{n-2},\bm{i}_{n-1})})\leq\cos(\theta)^{2}\cdot C(\rho_{1}^{(i_{1},\dots,i_{n-2})}).

A successive application of this bound yields the claimed bound in (73). ∎

D.6 Conditional independence for random shallow 1D circuits

Our study of conditional independence in Section D.5 and Section D.4 has focused on states that can be prepared by depth-22 quantum circuits. The first layer of gates in the circuit prepares entangled pairs of qubits. The second layer, followed by measurements in the computational basis, forms the two-qubit measurements that cause the entanglement swapping.

We presented two mechanisms for the emergence of conditionally-independent correlations after measurements. The first, as stated in Theorem D.13, occurs when partially entangled states are prepared in the first layer. The second, as stated in Corollary D.1, occurs when the two-qubit measurements are not maximally entangling.

In this section, we extend this analysis to the case of depth-DD one-dimensional quantum circuits, for any constant DD. We show that random shallow quantum circuits exhibit conditional independence due to both of the mechanisms stated above.

D.6.1 Setup

We slightly adjust the notation previously established in Definition D.5 for clarity. Initially, we consider two pairs of entangled qudits (dimension d0d_{0}) in the state |ψ⟩=|a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣\left|\psi\right\rangle=\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}. We then apply a rotation to this state, resulting in U𝖡𝖢⊗𝟙𝖠𝖣⋅|a⟩𝖠𝖡|b⟩𝖢𝖣U_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{AD}}\cdot\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}. Subsequently, we measure the 𝖡𝖢\mathsf{BC} subsystem in the computational basis. The probability of obtaining outcome i∈[d0]i\in[d_{0}] after measuring subsystem 𝖡\mathsf{B} but before measuring subsystem 𝖢\mathsf{C} is represented by pip_{i}. Conditioned on this outcome, the post-measurement state on 𝖠𝖡𝖢𝖣\mathsf{ABCD} is |ψi⟩\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle with ρ𝖠i\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}} denoting the reduced state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A}.

The Schmidt decomposition of the state |a⟩\left|a\right\rangle is given by |a⟩𝖠𝖡=∑k=1d0λk|k⟩𝖠|k⟩𝖡\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}=\sum_{k=1}^{d_{0}}\sqrt{\lambda_{k}}\left|k\right\rangle_{\mathsf{A}}\left|k\right\rangle_{\mathsf{B}}. Now consider an experiment where the state |k⟩𝖡|b⟩𝖢𝖣\left|k\right\rangle_{\mathsf{B}}\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}} is first rotated by U𝖡𝖢⊗𝟙𝖣U_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{D}} and then its subsystem 𝖡\mathsf{B} is measured in the computational basis and the outcome i∈[d0]i\in[d_{0}] is observed. The state |ϕi,k⟩𝖢𝖣\left|\phi_{i,k}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}} which describes the resulting post-measurement state can be expressed as

|ϕi,k⟩𝖢𝖣=1qi,k1/2(⟨i|𝖡⊗𝟙𝖢𝖣)⋅(U𝖡𝖢⊗𝟙𝖣)⋅|k⟩𝖡|b⟩𝖢𝖣,\displaystyle\left|\phi_{i,k}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}=\frac{1}{q_{i,k}^{1/2}}(\left\langle i\right|_{\mathsf{B}}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{CD}})\cdot(U_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{D}})\cdot\left|k\right\rangle_{\mathsf{B}}\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}, (74)

where the normalization factor qi,kq_{i,k} is defined by

qi,k=tr⁡[(|i⟩​⟨i|𝖡⊗𝟙𝖢𝖣)⋅(U𝖡𝖢⊗𝟙𝖣)⋅(|k⟩​⟨k|𝖡⊗|b⟩​⟨b|𝖢𝖣)⋅(U𝖡𝖢†⊗𝟙𝖠𝖣)].\displaystyle q_{i,k}=\operatorname{tr}[(|i\rangle\langle i|_{\mathsf{B}}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{CD}})\cdot(U_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{D}})\cdot(|k\rangle\langle k|_{\mathsf{B}}\otimes|b\rangle\langle b|_{\mathsf{CD}})\cdot(U_{\mathsf{BC}}^{\dagger}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{AD}})].

The post-measurment state |ψi⟩\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle resulting form measuring |a⟩AB⊗|b⟩CD\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathrm{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathrm{CD}} admits the following expression

|ψi⟩=1pi∑kλk​qi,k⋅|k⟩𝖠|i⟩𝖡|ϕi,k⟩𝖢𝖣, with pi=∑kλkqi,k.\displaystyle\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{p_{i}}}\sum_{k}\sqrt{\lambda_{k}q_{i,k}}\cdot|k\rangle_{\mathsf{A}}\left|i\right\rangle_{\mathsf{B}}|\phi_{i,k}\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}},\text{ with }p_{i}=\sum_{k}\lambda_{k}q_{i,k}. (75)

There is also a simpler interpretation to the above, in terms of a random variable 𝑿\bm{X} which is set to k∈[d0]k\in[d_{0}] with probability λk\lambda_{k}, and the measurement outcome 𝑰\bm{I}:

|ψi⟩=∑kPr⁡[𝑿=k|𝑰=i]⋅|k⟩𝖠|i⟩𝖡|ϕi,k⟩𝖢𝖣.\left|\psi_{i}\right\rangle=\sum_{k}\sqrt{\mathrm{Pr}[\bm{X}=k|\bm{I}=i]}\cdot\left|k\right\rangle_{\mathsf{A}}\left|i\right\rangle_{\mathsf{B}}\left|\phi_{i,k}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}}. (76)

D.6.2 Imperfect swapping from the top Schmidt coefficient

Our proof strategy is inspired by that of [54], which studies random depth-2 quantum circuits. We proceed by establishing a lower bound for the operator norm of the post-measurement reduced state. This approach demonstrates that the entanglement swapping measurements, resulting from the application of random shallow circuits, are ‘imperfect’ in a well-defined sense.

Definition D.14 (Imperfect entanglement swapping).

An entanglement swapping protocol on subsystems 𝖠𝖡𝖢𝖣\mathsf{ABCD} with post-measurement stated given by (74) is called ϵ\epsilon-imperfect if

mini,k,k′⁡|⟨ϕi,k|ϕi,k′⟩|2=ϵ>0.\min_{i,k,k^{\prime}}|\left\langle\phi_{i,k}\middle|\phi_{i,k^{\prime}}\right\rangle|^{2}=\epsilon>0.
Theorem D.15 (Bounding the operator norm, cf. [54]).

Following the application of an ϵ\epsilon-imperfect entanglement swapping, the average top Schmidt coefficient of the reduced state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} is bounded from below by

𝔼𝒊​‖𝝆𝖠𝒊‖∞≥(1−ϵ)⋅‖ρ𝖠‖∞+ϵ,\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}}{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}^{\bm{i}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}\geq(1-\epsilon)\cdot{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho_{\mathsf{A}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}+\epsilon, (77)

where ρ𝖠\rho_{\mathsf{A}} is the state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} prior to the measurements. In particular, this implies that unless ‖ρ𝖠‖∞=1{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho_{\mathsf{A}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}=1 we have 𝔼𝐢​‖𝛒𝖠𝐢‖∞>‖ρ𝖠‖∞\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}}{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}^{\bm{i}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}>{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho_{\mathsf{A}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty} for imperfect measurements.

Proof.

Since after measuring subsystem 𝖡\mathsf{B}, the post-measurement state on 𝖠𝖡𝖢𝖣\mathsf{ABCD} is pure and classical on subsystem 𝖡\mathsf{B}, it holds that ‖ρ𝖠i‖∞=‖ρ𝖢𝖣i‖∞{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{A}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}={|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho_{\mathsf{CD}}^{i}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty} where ρ𝖢𝖣i\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{CD}} is the reduced state on 𝖢𝖣\mathsf{CD} conditioned on observing outcome i∈[d0]i\in[d_{0}] upon measuring 𝖡\mathsf{B}. Using the expression (76), the reduced state ρ𝖢𝖣i\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{CD}} satisfies

‖ρ𝖢𝖣i‖∞\displaystyle{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{CD}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty} ≥maxk⟨ϕi,k|⋅ρ𝖢𝖣i⋅|ϕi,k⟩\displaystyle\geq\max_{k}\ \left\langle\phi_{i,k}\right|\cdot\rho^{i}_{\mathsf{CD}}\cdot\left|\phi_{i,k}\right\rangle
=maxk⁡(Pr⁡[𝑿=k|𝑰=i]+∑k′≠kPr⁡[X=k′|𝑰=i]⋅|⟨ϕi,k|ϕi,k′⟩|2)\displaystyle=\max_{k}\ (\mathrm{Pr}[\bm{X}=k|\bm{I}=i]+\sum_{k^{\prime}\neq k}\mathrm{Pr}[X=k^{\prime}|\bm{I}=i]\cdot|\left\langle\phi_{i,k}\middle|\phi_{i,k^{\prime}}\right\rangle|^{2})
≥maxk⁡(Pr⁡[𝑿=k|𝑰=i]+(1−Pr⁡[𝑿=k|𝑰=i])⋅ϵ)\displaystyle\geq\max_{k}\ (\mathrm{Pr}[\bm{X}=k|\bm{I}=i]+(1-\mathrm{Pr}[\bm{X}=k|\bm{I}=i])\cdot\epsilon) (78)

for any choice of kk. In expectation over i∈[d0]i\in[d_{0}] and picking kk to be the index of the top eigenvalue of the pre-measurement reduced state ρ\rho on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A}, we observe the claimed bound in (77).

∎

In our previous analysis, the measurement is only performed on subsystem 𝖡\mathsf{B}. Let |ψi​j⟩\left|\psi_{ij}\right\rangle denote the reduced state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} conditioned on observing outcomes i∈[d0]i\in[d_{0}] and j∈[d0]j\in[d_{0}] after measuring 𝖡𝖢\mathsf{BC}. We next show that a convexity argument ensures that on average, the top Schmidt coefficient ‖ρ𝖠(i,j)‖∞{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho_{\mathsf{A}}^{(i,j)}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty} strictly increases.

Corollary D.2.

Following the application of an ϵ\epsilon-imperfect entanglement swapping, the average top Schmidt coefficient of the reduced state on subsystem 𝖠\mathsf{A} is bounded from below by

𝔼𝒊,𝒋||𝝆𝖠(𝒊,𝒋)||∞≥𝔼𝒊​‖𝔼𝒋​𝝆𝖠(𝒊,𝒋)‖∞≥(1−ϵ)⋅‖ρA‖∞+ϵ\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i},\bm{j}}{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}^{(\bm{i},\bm{j})}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}\geq\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}}{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{j}}\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}^{(\bm{i},\bm{j})}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}\geq(1-\epsilon)\cdot{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho_{A}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}+\epsilon (79)

We now discuss how Haar random unitaries and low-depth, random quantum circuits give rise to imperfect entanglement swapping. Namely, we argue that in expectation over the randomness of the unitaries, these protocols are ϵ\epsilon-imperfect for some constant ϵ\epsilon, a function of the local dimension (in the Haar random case) and circuit depth.

In the upcoming analysis, it is convenient to use the following un-normalized version of the overlap between states |ϕi,k⟩\left|\phi_{i,k}\right\rangle and |ϕi,k′⟩\left|\phi_{i,k^{\prime}}\right\rangle for k≠k′k\neq k^{\prime} which are defined in (74):

f⁡(U𝖡𝖢,i,k,k′,σ𝖢):=qi,k⋅qi,k′⋅|⟨ϕi,k|ϕi,k′⟩|2\displaystyle f(U_{\mathsf{BC}},i,k,k^{\prime},\sigma_{\mathsf{C}}):=q_{i,k}\cdot q_{i,k^{\prime}}\cdot|\left\langle\phi_{i,k}\middle|\phi_{i,k^{\prime}}\right\rangle|^{2}
=tr𝖡𝖢,𝖡′​𝖢′⁡[(U𝖡𝖢†⊗U𝖡′​𝖢′†)​(|i⟩​⟨i|𝖡⊗|i⟩​⟨i|𝖡′⊗𝟙𝖢𝖢′)​(U𝖡𝖢⊗U𝖡′​𝖢′)⋅(|k⟩​⟨k′|B⊗σ𝖢⊗|k′⟩​⟨k|𝖡′⊗σ𝖢′)].\displaystyle=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathsf{BC},\mathsf{B^{\prime}C^{\prime}}}\bigg[(U^{\dagger}_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes U^{\dagger}_{\mathsf{\mathsf{B^{\prime}C^{\prime}}}})(|i\rangle\langle i|_{\mathsf{B}}\otimes|i\rangle\langle i|_{\mathsf{B^{\prime}}}\otimes\mathds{1}_{\mathsf{CC^{\prime}}})(U_{\mathsf{BC}}\otimes U_{\mathsf{B^{\prime}C^{\prime}}})\cdot\big(|k\rangle\langle k^{\prime}|_{B}\otimes\sigma_{\mathsf{C}}\otimes|k^{\prime}\rangle\langle k|_{\mathsf{B^{\prime}}}\otimes\sigma_{\mathsf{C^{\prime}}}\big)\bigg]. (80)

where

σ𝖢=tr𝖣⁡|b⟩​⟨b|𝖢𝖣\sigma_{\mathsf{C}}=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathsf{D}}|b\rangle\langle b|_{\mathsf{CD}}

is the reduced state on subsystem 𝖢\mathsf{C} of the original state |a⟩𝖠𝖡⊗|b⟩𝖢𝖣\left|a\right\rangle_{\mathsf{AB}}\otimes\left|b\right\rangle_{\mathsf{CD}} prior to the entanglement swapping measurement. The notion of ϵ\epsilon-imperfectness for an entanglement swapping protocol in Definition D.14 relies on establishing that mini,k,k′⁡|⟨ϕi,k|ϕi,k′⟩|2≥ϵ\min_{i,k,k^{\prime}}|\left\langle\phi_{i,k}\middle|\phi_{i,k^{\prime}}\right\rangle|^{2}\geq\epsilon. However, dealing with the normalization factors qi,kq_{i,k} and qi,k′q_{i,k^{\prime}}, turns out to be challenging when averaging over random choices of unitaries UU. In the next lemma, we show that one can instead directly lower bound the un-normalized version of the overlaps mini,k,k′∈[d0]⁡f⁡(U,i,k,k′,σ𝖢)≥ϵ\min_{i,k,k^{\prime}\in[d_{0}]}f(U,i,k,k^{\prime},\sigma_{\mathsf{C}})\geq\epsilon. This results in a looser (d0⋅ϵ)(d_{0}\cdot\epsilon)-imperfectness, but is sufficient for our application of establishing conditional independence.

Lemma D.16.

Suppose 𝔼𝐔​f​(𝐔,i,k,k′,σ𝖢)≥ϵ\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}}f(\bm{U},i,k,k^{\prime},\sigma_{\mathsf{C}})\geq\epsilon for all i∈[d0]i\in[d_{0}] and k≠k′∈[d0]k\neq k^{\prime}\in[d_{0}]. Then, we have

𝔼𝑼,𝒊​‖𝝆𝖠𝒊‖∞≥‖ρ𝖠‖∞⋅(1−d0⋅ϵ)+d0⋅ϵ\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U},\bm{i}}{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}^{\bm{i}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}\geq{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\rho_{\mathsf{A}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty}\cdot(1-d_{0}\cdot\epsilon)+d_{0}\cdot\epsilon (81)
Proof.

Following the proof of Theorem D.15 and using the notation in (74) and (75), we have that for all k∈[d0]k\in[d_{0}]

𝔼𝑼,𝒊​‖𝝆𝖠𝒊‖∞\displaystyle\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U},\bm{i}}{|\hskip-1.59016pt|\bm{\rho}_{\mathsf{A}}^{\bm{i}}|\hskip-1.59016pt|}_{\infty} ≥λk+∑k′≠k𝔼𝒊𝔼𝑼[⋅q𝒊,k′​λk′p𝒊⋅|⟨ϕ𝒊,k|ϕ𝒊,k′⟩|2]\displaystyle\geq\lambda_{k}+\sum_{k^{\prime}\neq k}\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}}\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}}\bigg[\cdot\frac{q_{\bm{i},k^{\prime}}\lambda_{k^{\prime}}}{p_{\bm{i}}}\cdot|\left\langle\phi_{\bm{i},k}\middle|\phi_{\bm{i},k^{\prime}}\right\rangle|^{2}\bigg]
=λk+∑k′≠kλk′⋅∑i𝔼𝑼​[f⁡(𝑼,i,k,k′,σ𝖢)qi,k]≥λk+∑k′≠kλk′⋅d0⋅ϵ\displaystyle=\lambda_{k}+\sum_{k^{\prime}\neq k}\lambda_{k^{\prime}}\cdot\sum_{i}\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}}\bigg[\frac{f(\bm{U},i,k,k^{\prime},\sigma_{\mathsf{C}})}{q_{i,k}}\bigg]\geq\lambda_{k}+\sum_{k^{\prime}\neq k}\lambda_{k^{\prime}}\cdot d_{0}\cdot\epsilon
=λk+(1−λk)⋅d0⋅ϵ.\displaystyle=\lambda_{k}+(1-\lambda_{k})\cdot d_{0}\cdot\epsilon. (82)

To arrive at the last inequality, we used the fact that qi,k≤1q_{i,k}\leq 1 and by assumption 𝔼𝑼​f​(𝑼,i,k,k′,σ𝖢)≥ϵ\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}}f(\bm{U},i,k,k^{\prime},\sigma_{\mathsf{C}})\geq\epsilon for all i∈[d0]i\in[d_{0}] and k≠k′∈[d0]k\neq k^{\prime}\in[d_{0}]. ∎

By sequentially repeating the result of Lemma D.16, we can establish a decay of conditional correlations along a chain of qudits that satisfy 𝔼𝑼​f​(𝑼,i,k,k′,σ𝖢)≥ϵ\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}}f(\bm{U},i,k,k^{\prime},\sigma_{\mathsf{C}})\geq\epsilon. To this end, consider the state ⊗k=1n|ak⟩𝖫k​𝖱k\otimes_{k=1}^{n}\left|a_{k}\right\rangle_{\mathsf{L}_{k}\mathsf{R}_{k}} where each subsystem has a local dimension d0d_{0}. Suppose each pair of registers (𝖱j,𝖫j+1)(\mathsf{R}_{j},\mathsf{L}_{j+1}) for j∈[n−1]j\in[n-1] are first rotated by a random unitary 𝑼𝒋\bm{U_{j}} and then measured in the computational basis. We denote the outcomes by (𝒊1,…,𝒊n−1)(\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1}) for 𝒊1,…,𝒊n−1∈[d0]×2\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1}\in[d_{0}]^{\times 2}. Given a random set of unitaries 𝑼𝟏,…,𝑼𝒏−𝟏\bm{U_{1}},\dots,\bm{U_{n-1}}, we let 𝝆1(𝒊1,…,𝒊j)\bm{\rho}_{1}^{(\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{j})} be the post-measurement state on subsystem 𝖫1\mathsf{L}_{1} upon the first jj measurements. Our goal is to upper bound 𝔼𝑼1,…,𝑼n−1​𝔼𝒊1,…,𝒊n−1​S​(𝝆1(𝒊1,…,𝒊n−1))\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}_{1},\dots,\bm{U}_{n-1}}\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1}}S(\bm{\rho}_{1}^{(\bm{i}_{1},\dots,\bm{i}_{n-1})}).

Corollary D.3 (Conditional independence for random 1D shallow circuits, restatement of Theorem II.3).

Consider the family of random depth-DD brickwork quantum circuits acting on a one-dimensional chain of qudits with the local dimension dd. I(𝖠i:𝖠j|𝖠i+1,…,𝖠j−1)≤e−Ω⁡(dist⁡(𝖠i,𝖠j))≤1/poly(n).\displaystyle I(\mathsf{A}_{i}:\mathsf{A}_{j}|\mathsf{A}_{i+1},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{j-1})\leq e^{-\Omega{\left(\mathrm{dist}(\mathsf{A}_{i},\mathsf{A}_{j})\right)}}\leq 1/\operatorname{poly}(n). (89)

for any 1≤i<j≤n′1\leq i<j\leq n^{\prime} with |i−j|>1|i-j|>1.

Proof.

We consider the setup of Proposition D.17. Given the stated choice of LL, the distance dist⁡(𝖠𝗂,𝖠𝗃)≥Ω⁡(log⁡(n))\mathrm{dist}(\mathsf{A_{i}},\mathsf{A_{j}})\geq\Omega(\log(n)) for any 1≤i<j≤n′1\leq i<j\leq n^{\prime}. We decompose the circuit into backward △\triangle and forward lightcones ▽\bigtriangledown as in Figure 3, and think of each subsystem 𝖠𝗂\mathsf{A_{i}} as a region consisting of an integer number of backward lightcones, along with two half-backward lightcones at its right and left boundaries.

Suppose we proceed to measure subsystems 𝖠i+1,…,𝖠j−1\mathsf{A}_{i+1},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{j-1}. We know from Lemma D.18 that shallow 1D quantum circuits satisfy 𝔼𝑼​f​(𝑼,i,k,k′,σ)≥ϵ\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}}f(\bm{U},i,k,k^{\prime},\sigma)\geq\epsilon with ϵ≳(4​d)−3​D\epsilon\gtrsim(4d)^{-3D} for any choice of reduced state σ\sigma. Following a lightcone argument, we see that, the measurement probabilities and the resulting entanglement between the unmeasured subsystems does not change by applying the gates in any of the forward lightcones ▽\bigtriangledown supported in regions 𝖠i\mathsf{A}_{i} and 𝖠j\mathsf{A}_{j}. This along with the data processing inequality applied to subsystems 𝖠1,…,𝖠i−1\mathsf{A}_{1},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{i-1} and 𝖠j+1,…,𝖠n′\mathsf{A}_{j+1},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{n^{\prime}}, shows that it suffices to apply our entanglement swapping analysis only to a part of the circuit consisting of the middle subsystems 𝖠i+1,…,𝖠𝗃−1\mathsf{A}_{i+1},\dots,\mathsf{A_{j}}-1 along with the qubits in the right boundary of 𝖠i\mathsf{A}_{i} and the left boundary of 𝖠j\mathsf{A}_{j}, independent of the measurement outcome in the rest of the circuit. Applying (85) and (48) implies that 𝔼𝑼I(𝖠i:𝖠𝗃|𝖠i+1,…,𝖠j−1)≤1nc0−1\mathbb{E\/}_{\bm{U}}I(\mathsf{A}_{i}:\mathsf{\mathsf{A}_{j}}|\mathsf{A}_{i+1},\dots,\mathsf{A}_{j-1})\leq\frac{1}{n^{c_{0}-1}}. An application of the Markov inequality and a union bound over the choice of regions 𝖠i\mathsf{A}_{i} and 𝖠j\mathsf{A}_{j} concludes the proof.
